minutes.headline: Committee drafted common questions for next week's three architect interviews; only adjournment was moved
minutes.summary: The building design committee prepared for interviews of three architect firms the following Wednesday. Members drafted shared questions on renovation experience, hazardous material assessment, budget control, funding success, timeline and subcontracting, and discussed reference checks, scoring and presentation logistics. Cost expectations for the project were also aired.

budget_items.topic: Design funding allocated by Town Meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted an amount allocated by Town Meeting and asked whether it acts as a target. Others said firms were chosen on qualifications and the contract is negotiated afterward.
Members discussed the conceptual cost and whether the firms' experience range fits, and a member said a wide public range had been floated earlier.
A member cited a municipal project that bid well over the engineer's estimate; members noted rising material prices and fewer bids on smaller projects.

what_happened.line: The building design committee agreed on a common list of about seven questions for all three architect firms, with members free to add their own.
The interview format was set: a 15-20 minute presentation, common questions, round-table questions, then public questions if time permits.
Members will use a time-warning flip card, and the chair will check the lapel mic, projector and podium placement with the town.
Reference calls will be chosen after the interviews, and the chair will ask about the process.
Members discussed whether the design funding set by Town Meeting acts as a target, and whether the firms' experience fits the conceptual cost range.

why_it_matters: The architect chosen shapes the design and cost of a town building project that residents will later be asked to fund, likely through Town Meeting votes and possibly a tax increase.
Committee discussion of rising material prices and fewer bids on smaller projects points to a mechanism by which final costs can exceed early estimates.
